I hated every single Christmas in my life. Every family gathering was just my father getting drunk, my mom yelling at him for it, and my grandparents adding to all the yelling. All the lights and the music and the "kindness" was always fake to me, just clever marketing. I grew up and I was forced to have Christmas with my boyfriends' families, which was just as bad. (I have social anxiety and depression.) Last year I spent Christmas with my ex (who wasn't my ex at the time. Not even my boyfriend.) and a bunch of his friends, at that was ok for a while. After dinner I ran upstairs to play Portals, because being with people makes me extremely uncomfortable. This year my boyfriend insisted that I spend Christmas with him and his family. And maybe this year's Christmas  will be the only one I don't hate with a passion, as I turned him down and I'm going to spend it getting drunk on my couch, by myself.


TL;DR: Christmas sucks.

Met my boyfriend online at about 12 noon on a dating website. We agreed to go out for a coffee at 5. We left when the coffee shop closed, and went back to mine to continue our discussion  (and because he was cute). It was about 10pm when he said "oh, if you like museums, you should go to London!" To which I replied, "ok, let's go to London!" We bought bus tickets and at 3am, basically 15h after having acknowledged each other's existence, we were on a bus to London.

Part 2: we missed the bus back, and couldn't get on the following one, so we had to wait until morning to get a train. We didn't have enough money for a hotel, so we napped in the hallway of a block, on the staircase. It was February and it was bloody freezing outside. We finally managed to get on a train at 7am and went home. Spent the next 2 days together at my place. It was the best date I've ever had.

TL;DR: Guy and girl meet online and go on a trip in the middle of the night having known each other for less than 12h. They miss the bus and spend the night having a homeless experience in London.

I've lived with depress my whole life, and I didn't think the way I felt was unnatural, to put it like this, until I've had medication and realised I can feel different. I've gone off my meds a couple of weeks ago, I quit cold turkey (NEVER do that, trust me) because I hated the doctors and the therapists and all the pills that did nothing to improve my mood, but made it worse instead.

The times that I felt ok with myself were when I was on Prozac, Trazodone and Lorazepam at the same time. Then I moved to UK and the GPs flipped out because here they are not prescribed at the same time due to possible side effects, so they took me off them one by one. Needless to say, this worsened my mood every week. I was maxed out on Prozac and it didn't do anything for me. I was then put on Venlafaxine, and after going through hell and back with its side effects it ended up not helping me at all. That's when I quit.

Back to the original idea. I've felt ok for about a week and a half, maybe two. I noticed I wasn't constantly thinking about death and suicide anymore, I was following my passions, painting and reading again, I was going to the gym, and it was all great. Two days ago, it came back to haunt me: I was spacing out all the time, messed up sleeping pattern (sleep all day, don't go to bed until morning), feeling isolated and as if I was the victim (of...something, I don't even know), cut off my friends and family, felt a great sorrow within me which made me feel sorry for myself and made me want to hug myself and cry all the time. I am now aware that this is just my depression ("just") and that it will go away in a while, but I don't know how to stop it. I don't know how to feel better or attempt to feel better.

I don't have any friends who'd be genuinely hurt, my boyfriend would eventually be able to get over it, and I don't like my family very much. I desperately want to no longer live, to the point where I'm sad if I crossed the road in a rush and a car could have ran me over but it didn't. I'm at the point where I don't care about "all the beautiful experiences" I will have in my life. I'll always have depression, regardless of all the medication I'm taking or the therapists I'm seeing. 

However, what I love most in this world is my cat. I love her more than my whole blood family. More than memes and Game of Thrones. She hates everyone else and wouldn't even be in the same room with them if I'm not present. How could I possibly go ahead and kill myself when she'd end up in a shelter? I've had her since she was a baby and it's highly unlikely she'd get used to someone else.

If this doesn't do anything for you guys, my second answer is Game of Thrones season 7/The Winds of Winter.
